title.en: Distinguish in situ and ex situ conservation
Explain biodiversity hotspots and name India's hotspots
Describe protected areas, sacred groves and ex situ methods

say.en: A tiger in a zoo is alive, but a tiger reserve saves the tiger together with its whole forest. Conservation works both inside and outside natural habitats. In this lesson: Distinguish in situ and ex situ conservation.
Explain biodiversity hotspots and name India's hotspots.
Describe protected areas, sacred groves and ex situ methods.

body.en: When we conserve and protect the whole ecosystem, its biodiversity at all levels is protected: we save the entire forest to save the tiger. This is in situ (on site) *conservation*. Since there are more species to save than resources allow, the most species-rich areas get priority. Biodiversity hotspots are regions with very high levels of species richness and a high degree of endemism (species confined to that region and not found anywhere else). Initially 25 hotspots were identified; nine more were added later, bringing the total to 34. Three of these, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and the Himalaya, cover our country's exceptionally high biodiversity regions. Although all the biodiversity hotspots together cover less than 2 per cent of the Earth's land area, the number of species they collectively harbour is extremely high, and strict protection of these hotspots could reduce the ongoing mass extinctions by almost 30 per cent. In India, ecologically unique and biodiversity-rich regions are legally protected as biosphere reserves, national parks and sanctuaries: India now has 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks and 448 wildlife sanctuaries. India also has a history of religious and cultural traditions that emphasised protection of nature: tracts of forest were set aside and all trees and wildlife within them were venerated and protected. Such sacred groves are found in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya, the Aravalli Hills of Rajasthan, the Western Ghat regions of Karnataka and Maharashtra, and the Sarguja, Chanda and Bastar areas of Madhya Pradesh. In Meghalaya, the sacred groves are the last refuges for a large number of rare and threatened plants.

points.en: 25 + 9 = 34 *hotspots*; cover < 2% of land; protection could cut extinctions by ~30%
India: Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, Himalaya
14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks, 448 wildlife sanctuaries
Sacred groves: Khasi and Jaintia Hills, Aravallis, Western Ghats, Bastar

narration.en: In situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats. Hotspots, with high species richness and endemism, get priority; India has three: the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and the Himalaya. India also protects biosphere reserves, national parks, sanctuaries and sacred groves.

title.en: Saving tigers in situ and ex situ

narration.en: A tiger population grows logistically up to the number its reserve can support (about one tiger per 10 km² of good forest here), while poaching removes a share every year. Protecting the reserve (in situ conservation, as in Project Tiger) cuts poaching; releasing zoo-bred animals (ex situ) adds a few each year.

title.en: Board: in situ and ex situ

say.en: We can protect species where they live, in situ, or take them out of their habitat to safe places, ex situ.
In situ: 34 biodiversity hotspots worldwide, three of them covering India. India also has 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks, 448 wildlife sanctuaries and many sacred groves.
Ex situ: zoos, botanical gardens and safari parks, and new tools: cryopreserved gametes, in vitro fertilisation, tissue culture and seed banks.
Countries act together too: the Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro in 1992, and the Johannesburg summit of 2002 where 190 countries pledged to slow biodiversity loss.

title.en: Ex situ conservation and global efforts

body.en: In *ex situ* (off site) conservation, threatened animals and plants are taken out of their natural habitat and placed in special settings where they can be protected and given special care. Zoological parks, botanical gardens and wildlife safari parks serve this purpose. Many animals that have become extinct in the wild continue to be maintained in zoological parks. Gametes of threatened species can now be preserved in viable and fertile condition for long periods using cryopreservation techniques; eggs can be fertilised in vitro; and plants can be propagated using tissue culture methods. Seeds of different genetic strains of commercially important plants can be kept for long periods in seed banks. Biodiversity knows no political boundaries, so conservation is a collective responsibility of all nations. The historic Convention on Biological Diversity ("The Earth Summit") held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 called upon all nations to take appropriate measures for conservation of biodiversity and sustainable utilisation of its benefits. In a follow-up, the World Summit on Sustainable Development held in 2002 in Johannesburg, South Africa, 190 countries pledged their commitment to achieve by 2010 a significant reduction in the current rate of biodiversity loss at global, regional and local levels.

points.en: *Ex situ*: zoological parks, botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks
Cryopreservation of gametes; in vitro fertilisation; tissue culture
Seed banks for genetic strains of crops
Earth Summit, Rio de Janeiro 1992; Johannesburg 2002: 190 countries

narration.en: Ex situ conservation protects species outside their habitat: zoos, botanical gardens, safari parks, cryopreserved gametes, tissue culture and seed banks. Globally, the Earth Summit at Rio in 1992 and the Johannesburg summit in 2002 committed nations to slowing biodiversity loss.
narration.kn: ಪರಸ್ಥಾನ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ ಪ್ರಭೇದಗಳನ್ನು ಆವಾಸದ ಹೊರಗೆ ರಕ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: ಮೃಗಾಲಯ, ಸಸ್ಯೋದ್ಯಾನ, ಸಫಾರಿ ಉದ್ಯಾನ, ಶೀತಲೀಕೃತ ಜನನಕೋಶಗಳು, ಅಂಗಾಂಶ ಕೃಷಿ ಮತ್ತು ಬೀಜ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕ್‌ಗಳು. 1992ರ ರಿಯೋ ಭೂ ಶೃಂಗಸಭೆ ಮತ್ತು 2002ರ ಜೊಹಾನ್ಸ್‌ಬರ್ಗ್ ಶೃಂಗಸಭೆ ದೇಶಗಳನ್ನು ಜೀವವೈವಿಧ್ಯ ನಷ್ಟ ತಗ್ಗಿಸಲು ಬದ್ಧಗೊಳಿಸಿದವು.

Ex situ: zoos, botanical gardens, safari parks, cryopreservation, seed banks. Earth Summit, Rio 1992; Johannesburg 2002.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಸ್ವಸ್ಥಾನ: ಇಡೀ ಆವಾಸವನ್ನು ರಕ್ಷಿಸುವುದು; ಹಾಟ್‌ಸ್ಪಾಟ್, ಜೈವಿಕ ಮೀಸಲು, ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಉದ್ಯಾನ, ಅಭಯಾರಣ್ಯ, ದೇವರಕಾಡು. 34 ಹಾಟ್‌ಸ್ಪಾಟ್‌ಗಳು; ಭಾರತ: ಪಶ್ಚಿಮ ಘಟ್ಟ ಮತ್ತು ಶ್ರೀಲಂಕಾ, ಇಂಡೋ-ಬರ್ಮಾ, ಹಿಮಾಲಯ. ಪರಸ್ಥಾನ: ಮೃಗಾಲಯ, ಸಸ್ಯೋದ್ಯಾನ, ಸಫಾರಿ ಉದ್ಯಾನ, ಶೀತಲೀಕರಣ, ಬೀಜ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕ್. ಭೂ ಶೃಂಗಸಭೆ, ರಿಯೋ 1992; ಜೊಹಾನ್ಸ್‌ಬರ್ಗ್ 2002.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. In situ: protect the whole habitat; hotspots, biosphere reserves, national parks, sanctuaries, sacred groves.
